### TCP state machine: a normal flow (client)

*  CLOSED → SYN_SENT (via open, causing sending SYN)
*  SYN_SENT → ESTABLISHED (via SYN+ACK, causing sending ACK)
*  ESTABLISHED → FIN_WAIT_1 (via close, causing sending FIN)
*  FIN_WAIT_1 → CLOSING (via FIN, causing sending ACK)
*  CLOSING → TIME_WAIT (via ACK)

### connection close {.smaller}

::::: {.columns}

:::: {.column width=50%}

![](/sockets/tcp-state-diagram-wiki.svg)

[figure: dnet/Nestea_Zen/Wikimedia Commons]{.mycredit}

::::

:::: {.column width=50%}

* each side gets to close separately
* FIN (I want to close) + ACK [of FIN] (confirm close) 
<hr class="vspace" />
* ACK side needs to wait just in case FIN resent 
   * keep port number from being reused
   * (if reused, could "close" future connection)
   * TIME_WAIT state

::::

:::::

### RST 


* RST (reset) flag often used to respond to unexpected packets
* example: data packet for never-established connection
